sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Whole screenshot script
sections.what: Reads the feature id and page pairs, optionally starts the server with the design gallery switch, opens each page at two widths and two themes, signs in if credentials are set, and saves a screenshot for each combination.
sections.why: Creates repeatable visual evidence for each feature in one command.
sections.watch_out: The design gallery switch is turned on for the server this script starts, so screenshots can show content that normal users never see.

summary: Takes screenshots of chosen app pages in light and dark mode at two screen widths, and saves them as visual evidence for a feature.
purpose: Gives a visual record of how a feature looks, for review or documentation.
why: Lets the owner see how a page renders without running the app.
how: Optionally starts the production server with a design gallery switch on, then for each page name and path it opens a browser at two widths and two colour themes, optionally signs in first, takes a screenshot, and saves it to a folder named after the feature.
inputs: A feature id, pairs of name and path on the command line, optional sign-in email and password from environment settings, the base address, and a full-page switch.
outputs: PNG images in docs/evidence/<feature-id>/, one per page, width and theme, and a console line for each file.
risks: The design gallery switch is set for the server this script starts, so the pages may show gallery-only content. Sign-in details come from environment settings and are typed into the page.
debug: If the images are blank, check the page path and that the app is built. If sign-in fails, check the login field labels and the environment settings. If the folder is missing, check write access to docs.
